newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-LIONS WEAK AT FLY-HALF,FULL-BACK--NAAS.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-LIONS WEAK AT FLY-HALF,FULL-BACK--NAAS.

text.p: Former Springbok captain Naas Botha said on Wednesday the British Lions, while being a very good squad, could be exposed in the key positions of fly-half and full-back.

Botha said he was surprised that England's South African-born fly-half Mike Catt -- also a versatile utility back -- had not been selected for the Lions tour of South Africa in late May, June and early July this year.

Speaking on television in South Africa after the live announcement of the 35-man British Lions tour squad on Wednesday, Botha said: "The two positions where they (the Lions) could find themselves in trouble are at full-back and at fly-half.
"At fly-half, they haven't got a major star and, at full-back, we're looking at Neil Jenkins -- but are we looking at Jenkins as a kicker or as a full-back?
"As a kicker, he's one of the best in the world but, as a full-back, he's certainly not in the same as league as Andre Joubert, for example."

Only two full-backs were named in the Lions squad on Wednesday -- Jenkins of Wales and England's Tim Stimpson. Veteran Welsh fly-half Jonathan Davies was also overlooked for Lions honours; the chosen stand-off halves were Scotland's Gregor Townsend and England's Paul Grayson.

"Townsend is a talented player but, in my mind, he is a centre rather than a fly-half. When the pressure was really on Townsend during this year's Five Nations, he tried to run Scotland out of trouble and wasn't too successful," Botha said.
"I'm very surprised Mike Catt hasn't made it as I was impressed with his last match for England in the Five Nations. He made all his kicks and he has added more dimension to his fly-half game."

But, overall, Botha was impressed with the strength of the British Lions tour party and felt that the choice of English lock Martin Johnson as captain -- in spite of no previous experience -- was a good one.

"A season ago, I thought there was a big gap between southern and northern hemisphere rugby. But they are now a lot better organised in the northern hemisphere and I was impressed with much of what I saw in this year's Five Nations championship.
"Also, in pooling together the four home unions, they can certainly put 15 guys on the field who can give us a very good series here in South Africa. It's a very good squad.
"As for Martin Johnson as captain, he might have no previous experience as a leader but he has the right sort of character. I think he's a good choice."
